diagnosis.hypothesis: At 02:30:50Z ledger-consumer was recreated with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, which appears to book every Kafka message without deduplicating on event_id. The provider resends webhooks until acknowledged, and webhook-receiver publishes each resend as a new message at a new offset, which consumers are expected to absorb. The naive handler posts each copy instead. 7 events were posted 2-3 times: 6 payment.succeeded duplicates inflated provider_clearing, and a duplicated refund.succeeded (evt_000288, pay_000217) pulled that payment below the provider. Net: the ledger is $461.00 ahead. Each duplicate is a full double-entry posting, so the ledger stays balanced, and payments and refunds still match. Left open: the previous LEDGER_HANDLER value, why the provider resent these events (likely slow acks around restarts), and whether all 7 duplicates came after 02:30:50 (I checked 2).

evidence.shows: The symptom is confirmed after the check settled. posted_exactly_once fails with 7 events posted 2 or 3 times (evt_000308 three times). matches_provider is off by +$461.00. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider.
ledger-consumer was recreated at 02:30:50Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 17 seconds before the alert. It is the only service changed after the 02:29:18 stack start.
ledger-consumer posted evt_000308 ($131.93) three times, at 02:31:04-02:31:05, from offsets 100, 101 and 103 of provider-events/0, each under a different trace.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times, at offsets 100, 101 and 103. These are provider redeliveries, each published as a separate message, not a Kafka replay.
evt_000251 was posted twice, at 02:30:50.7 (offset 73) and 02:30:51.4 (offset 76), right after the naive handler was deployed.

proposed_fix.summary: Redeploy ledger-consumer with its previous idempotent LEDGER_HANDLER, one that records each posted event_id in the same DB transaction as the posting and skips repeats. Then do a data repair: reverse the extra postings found by money_check, keeping the first posting of each event. The known extras are transactions 255, 266, 272, 273 and 297, plus the remaining duplicates of evt_000298 and evt_000308 from the full evidence list. Post them as compensating entries rather than deleting rows. Re-run money_check to confirm both invariants pass.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The redeploy briefly pauses ledger posting. Kafka lag grows and then catches up, and no events are lost because offsets are committed per consumer group. The reversals touch only the 7 affected payments' ledger entries. Reversing the wrong transaction would mis-state a real posting, so match each reversal by event_id against money_check's transaction_ids.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the restored handler misbehaves (stalls or dead-letters valid events), redeploy the current image and settings. Kafka retains the events, so they can be reprocessed from consumer-group offsets. Compensating entries can be undone with offsetting entries. Re-run money_check after any change.
